text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Some 900,000 hectares of grain including 220,000 hectares of barley and 680.000 hectares of milling wheat were sown in Bulgaria by November 1, the newspaper said quoting official data of Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry.

-- Two Russian companies and a business grouping based in Switzerland are interested in buying the Bulgarian state fork-lifting truck producer Balkankar Holding, Balkankar executive director Iliya Ivanovski said.
-- Bulgaria's State Reconstruction and Development Fund/SRDF/ will guarantee payments on grain imports from France and Argentina amounting to some $10 million, SRDF senior official said.
-- Moody's Investors Service said that Bulgaria's slow progress and heavy debt burden were shown in its B3 sovereign ceiling rating and Caa ceiling for bank deposits.

-- The International Monetary Fund /IMF/ has proposed introduction of currency board in Bulgaria, IMF European Department Director Michael Deppler said after meetings with representatives of Bulgaria's major political forces.
-- The European Union Phare programme extended some $2.1 million for the reconstruction of Bulgaria's Danube River Port of Rousse.

-- Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry has introduced minimum export prices for cooking oil as follows: for non-refined cooking oil in bulks - $450 per tonne, for refined cooking oil in bulks - $650 per tonne and for bottled refined cooking oil $850 per tonne, deputy agriculture minister Dimo Uzunov said.
-- Bulgaria's deputy transport minister Vasil Rangelov will discuss with his Yugoslav counterpart in Sofia today lifting of road charges in the two countries.
-- The state commercial Biochim Bank posted 650 million levs profit for October and 11.9 billion levs profit for the first ten months of 1996, Biochim executive director Stefan Doichinov said.

-- Bulgaria's Central Electoral Committee /CEC/ is expected to announce today the official results of the second round of the presidential elections, held on November 3, CEC spokeswoman Iliana Risova said.
